numberOfTests.description: the number of test vectors in this test

HpkeSequenceTestGroup.description: HPKE base-mode decryption of a SEQUENCE of messages on one context (RFC 9180). Each group fixes one (KEM, KDF, AEAD) ciphersuite. HPKE encryption is stateful and ordered: the recipient runs SetupBaseR once with enc, then calls Open once per message, and the AEAD nonce for sequence number i is base_nonce XOR I2OSP(i, Nn). Each test case carries one encapsulation (enc) and an ordered list of decryptions; the implementation opens them in the given order against a single context. This exercises nonce evolution (including sequence numbers above 255), rejection of out-of-order or replayed ciphertexts, and retry after a rejected ciphertext (a failed Open does not advance the sequence number), which single-shot cases cannot cover.

type.description: A legacy field, test files contain only one type per file

kemId.description: The two-byte HPKE KEM identifier from the IANA HPKE KEM registry (RFC 9180, extended by draft-ietf-hpke-pq-05)

kdfId.description: The two-byte HPKE KDF identifier (RFC 9180 Table 3)

aeadId.description: The two-byte HPKE AEAD identifier (RFC 9180 Table 5)

comment.description: A brief description of the test case

skRm.description: The serialized recipient private key (SerializePrivateKey of skR). For ML-KEM KEMs this is the 64-byte d || z seed; for DHKEM(X25519) it is the 32-byte unclamped scalar (see skEm).

pkRm.description: The serialized recipient public key (SerializePublicKey of pkR), derivable from skRm and provided for convenience

ikmE.description: Optional. The 32-byte randomness input to deterministic encapsulation (ikmE in the RFC 9180 Appendix A test vectors; the input to EncapDerand in draft-ietf-hpke-hpke-05 Appendix C.1). For DHKEM(X25519) it is the DeriveKeyPair input for the sender's ephemeral key pair, (skE, pkE) = DeriveKeyPair(ikmE); for ML-KEM (draft-ietf-hpke-pq-05) it is the randomness m passed to FIPS 203 ML-KEM.Encaps_internal. When present, deterministic encapsulation reproduces enc and the whole ct sequence. Present for cases whose decryptions are all valid; absent when any decryption is invalid.

skEm.description: Optional, DHKEM only. The sender's ephemeral private key skEm = SerializePrivateKey(skE), where (skE, pkE) = DeriveKeyPair(ikmE) and SerializePrivateKey is the identity for X25519 (draft-ietf-hpke-hpke-05 Section 7.1.2). Provided for deterministic-encapsulation test hooks that take the raw ephemeral private key rather than ikmE. Present exactly when ikmE is present for a DHKEM; absent for ML-KEM, which has no ephemeral key pair. For X25519 this is the unclamped 32-byte string that DeriveKeyPair returns, matching the RFC 9180 Appendix A test vectors. The text of RFC 9180 Section 7.1.2 requires SerializePrivateKey to clamp, so an implementation that follows it (e.g. Go crypto/hpke PrivateKey.Bytes) re-serializes the key to different bytes; compare public keys or results, not re-serialized private keys. X25519 treats clamped and unclamped scalars identically (RFC 7748 Section 5); an API that requires a clamped scalar needs the key clamped before import. See doc/hpke.md.

info.description: The HPKE info string bound into the key schedule

enc.description: The KEM encapsulated key (Nenc bytes) consumed once by SetupBaseR before opening the sequence

decryptions.description: The ordered messages to Open against the single SetupBaseR context, one Open call per entry, each with AEAD nonce base_nonce XOR I2OSP(sequenceNumber, Nn).

sequenceNumber.description: The context sequence number at which this ciphertext is opened (0-based): the number of successful Opens before this entry. A failed Open does not advance the sequence number (RFC 9180 Section 5.2), so an entry that follows an invalid one is opened at the same sequence number.

aad.description: The additional authenticated data passed to Open for this message

ct.description: The AEAD sealed message (ciphertext || tag) to open at this sequence number

pt.description: The expected recovered plaintext when result is valid; empty otherwise

result.description: valid: the context must behave exactly as listed in decryptions (each entry's result applies at its sequenceNumber)
